findings.clinical_note: Low RBC count with normal hemoglobin and hematocrit suggests early normocytic anemia or possible lab artifact; warrants further evaluation (iron studies, B12, reticulocyte count).
Prediabetes; upward trend indicates progression toward diabetes; consider lifestyle modification and repeat testing.
Mild hyperchloremia; together with falling CO2 may reflect non‑anion gap metabolic acidosis.
Bicarbonate at lower end of normal and decreasing, may indicate developing metabolic acidosis.
Slightly elevated MPV suggests increased platelet turnover or activation.
Within normal range; upward trend still within limits.

panel_patterns.interpretation: Mild hyperchloremia with low‑normal bicarbonate and a decreasing CO2 trend suggest a developing non‑anion gap metabolic acidosis; monitor electrolytes and acid‑base status.
Low RBC count with normal hemoglobin/hematocrit and elevated MPV indicates possible early normocytic anemia with increased platelet turnover.
